items.title: UK GDPR, Article 30: Records of processing activities
items.why: The nearest thing in UK law to a register duty: a written record of purposes, categories of data and recipients. Source of the figure (250 staff, Art. 30(5)). It does not ask for a description of how a system works or for a named owner. No outstanding changes shown; the only post-2020 amendment is 'Commission' in Art. 30(4), dated 30 September 2026.

items.title: UK GDPR, Article 5: Principles relating to processing of personal data
items.why: The accountability principle: the controller must be able to demonstrate compliance. Wording of 5(2) unchanged by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, which added Art. 5(3).

items.title: Data protection audit framework, Artificial intelligence toolkit: Governance and accountability in AI
items.locator: Control measure 'Information flows across the entire supply chain have been comprehensively mapped', under 'Risk'
items.why: Source of the quotation. Links poor internal knowledge to possible breach of Articles 5(1)(f), 5(2) and 30. Carries the 'under review' banner following the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; the page shows no publication date, so the year is the year it was read. Covers data protection only.

items.title: Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) Mandatory Scope and Exemptions Policy
items.why: States that the standard was mandated across government departments on 6 February 2024, and which arm's-length bodies and tools are in scope. Central government only; it does not bind companies.

items.title: UK Corporate Governance Code 2024
items.locator: Provision 29 and footnote 9 (PDF p. 14); application paragraph in the Introduction (PDF p. 6)
items.why: The board declaration on effectiveness of material controls, applying to financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2026. Applies to listed companies on a comply or explain basis. It does not mention AI or registers.

items.title: The hidden risks of shadow AI
items.locator: Sections 'What is shadow AI?' and 'What are the cyber security risks of shadow AI?'
items.why: Official definition of AI use that sits outside approved systems, and the loss of visibility it causes. The 71% figure it repeats comes from a supplier's survey, not from the NCSC, and is not used.
